scored.query: Do online sellers need to display a BIR Registration Seal Badge on their shop profiles or websites?
scored.context:
[1] RMC NO. 38-2026, p.3 (2026) · OCR
6. To ensure consistent and proper online display of the BER Registration Seal Badge on
websites, mobile applications, online shops and e-commerce platforms, the following
guidelines shall apply:

6.1 Only the BIR Registration Seal Badge shall be posted on the taxpayer’s official
website, mobile application, online shop, or e-commerce platform profile page. (refer
to Annex B).

6.2 Taxpayers are not required to upload their entire registration document or the full page
where the badge appears. Taxpayers may crop, scan, or extract only the BIR
Registration Seal Badge image for the purpose of uploading or posting it to their
official website, mobile application, online shop, or e-commerce platform profile
page. (refer to Annex B).

---

[2] RMC NO. 38-2026, p.2 (2026) · OCR
RMC NO. 38-2026
ay?

or with online presence, including but not limited to professionals or persons offering their
services through online website, e-commerce platforms or mobile applications, bloggers,
vloggers, live streamers, content creators, influencers, and individuals earning through online
views, advertisements, affiliate commissions, brand sponsorships, or similar monetized digital
activities.

To address taxpayers’ concems over the online disclosure of sensitive information
contained in their COR/eCOR, the BIR shall issue a BIR Registration Seal Badge (Annex
A) to be displayed on the seller’s/content creator’s/online influencer’s website, online
page/platform, e-commerce shop, in lieu of the BIR COR/eCOR.

Policies and Guidelines

---

[3] RMC NO. 38-2026, p.1 (2026) · OCR
In addition, Section 5(H) of RR No. 7-2024 and Section 7 of RR No. 15-2024 further
require the posting of proof of registration by sellers/merchants on their online websites, e-
commerce or e-marketplace pages, and other platforms. In this regard, online businesses,
sellers or merchants and service providers operating a business or with sales transactions
through a website, social media or any digital or electronic means shall display conspicuously
the electronic copy of their BER COR/eCOR on their website, account or profile pages of
the e-commerce platform or mobile application, where it is clearly visible and easily accessible
to buyers or customers.

---

[4] RMC NO. 38-2026, p.2 (2026) · OCR
Policies and Guidelines

1. The BIR Registration Seal Badge serves as proof of registration for businesses engaged
in online selling of goods or services, and e-commerce activities. It is issued together with
the BIR COR/eCOR and is intended to be posted on the taxpayer’s website, online store
or platform, mobile application, social media business page, or e-commerce seller profile
in heu of posting of copy of the BIR COR/eCOR.

---

[5] RMC NO. 38-2026, p.2 (2026) · OCR
4. Taxpayers are not required to replace their existing BIR COR/eCOR that does not contain
a QR Code; however, they are encouraged to update or replace the same for the purposes
of securing a BIR Registration Seal Badge. Taxpayers who are required to post online a
proof of their BIR registration shall secure a BIR Registration Seal Badge with the
Bureau’s Revenue District Office where they are registered by updating their registration
information, or secure it online via ORUS by updating their registration information and
paying the P30.00 Loose Documentary Stamp Tax (DST). 00 00 01 A T

scored.answer:
Yes. Online sellers and other taxpayers with an online presence are required to display the BIR Registration Seal Badge on their website, online store or platform, mobile application, social media business page, or e-commerce seller profile — in lieu of posting a copy of the BIR COR/eCOR [4][2].

Only the BIR Registration Seal Badge should be posted on the taxpayer's official website, mobile application, online shop, or e-commerce platform profile page [1]. Taxpayers are not required to upload their entire registration document or the full page where the badge appears; they may crop, scan, or extract only the badge image for posting [1].

scored.answer:
Oo, bawal at ilegal na ang offshore gaming operations o POGO sa Pilipinas. Ito ay dahil sa **Republic Act (RA) No. 12312**, na nagbabawal at nagdedeklara ng offshore gaming operations sa bansa bilang ilegal, at pinawalang-bisa ang RA No. 11590 (ang batas na nagbubuwis sa POGO) [1].

Sa ilalim ng batas na ito, ang mga POGO, POGO gaming content providers, POGO accredited service providers, at POGO local gaming agents na binawi ang lisensya ay mananatiling may pananagutan sa lahat ng buwis, bayarin, at iba pang singil hanggang sa huling araw ng kanilang operasyon [1]. Bukod dito, kahit binawi na ang lisensya at nagsara na ang operasyon, magsasagawa pa rin ng audit ang BIR upang matukoy ang anumang pananagutan sa buwis [2].

answer_relevance.original_query: Bawal at ilegal na ba talaga ang offshore gaming o POGO sa Pilipinas ngayon?
generated_questions: Legal ba ang offshore gaming operations o POGO sa Pilipinas?
Ano ang epekto ng Republic Act No. 12312 sa mga POGO sa bansa?
Ano ang mangyayari sa mga POGO na binawi ang lisensya sa usaping buwis?

row.query: Bawal at ilegal na ba talaga ang offshore gaming o POGO sa Pilipinas ngayon?

sagot.answer:
Oo, bawal at ilegal na ang offshore gaming operations o POGO sa Pilipinas. Ito ay dahil sa **Republic Act (RA) No. 12312**, na nagbabawal at nagdedeklara ng offshore gaming operations sa bansa bilang ilegal, at pinawalang-bisa ang RA No. 11590 (ang batas na nagbubuwis sa POGO) [1].

Sa ilalim ng batas na ito, ang mga POGO, POGO gaming content providers, POGO accredited service providers, at POGO local gaming agents na binawi ang lisensya ay mananatiling may pananagutan sa lahat ng buwis, bayarin, at iba pang singil hanggang sa huling araw ng kanilang operasyon [1]. Bukod dito, kahit binawi na ang lisensya at nagsara na ang operasyon, magsasagawa pa rin ng audit ang BIR upang matukoy ang anumang pananagutan sa buwis [2].
